prompt: Which single addition to the ORASHI record would clear the blocking item about a clause marked conformant with no evidence reference?
options: An assessor's name recorded on clause 6.1.3
An internal audit examination of clause 7.5.3
An evidence reference recorded on clause 5.2
A written justification recorded on clause 4.4
explanation: Clause 5.2 claims conformity with its evidence record false, and missingEvidenceParts prints evidence reference for it. Its date and assessor are already there, since it reads assessed true.

prompt: An assessor finds clause 7.2 failing and has no document to point to. Can the verdict go on the register?
options: Yes: Nonconformant with a date and an assessor is allowed with no evidence reference.
No: every clause verdict needs evidence, a date and an assessor before it stands.
Only as Partially conformant, which asks for less on the record than Nonconformant.
Only once an audit finding has been raised and recorded against the clause.
explanation: The digest prints Nonconformant with a date and an assessor: ALLOWED. Partially conformant asks for all three, as Conformant does. A problem needs less on the record than a claim of conformity.

prompt: An ISO 45001:2018 register sets a clause to Not applicable on both fields and gives no reason. What does the refusal name?
options: §4.3 of ISO 45001:2018, as the ISO 9001:2015 sentence cites its own clause
No standard at all, since only ISO 9001:2015 is ever named in the refusal
ISO 14001:2015, as the standard the ORASHI register itself is kept against
ISO 45001:2018, in the shape of the ISO 14001:2015 sentence
explanation: "Say why this requirement of ISO 45001:2018 does not apply. A requirement determined not applicable keeps its justification on record." Rule R5: a sentence names the register's own standard.

prompt: Clause 7.5.3 carries evidence, a date and an assessor behind its Conformant status. Which gate did it pass, and which count still leaves it out?
options: It passed canSetClauseStatus, and coverage still reads it never examined.
It passed the lead auditor check, and the evidenced count still leaves it out.
It passed canReportAudit, and the conformant count still leaves it out.
It passed canSetClauseStatus, and the evidenced count leaves it out.
explanation: The register verdict is the owner's assessment; coverage asks whether a counting internal audit examined the clause. ISA-2025-003 examined 7.5.3 on 2025-11-12 and was Cancelled, so it reads never.

prompt: At 2026-10-15, which ORASHI clause reads review overdue true?
options: 6.1.2, next review 2026-11-02, 18 days from the as-of date
7.2, next review 2027-01-31, still Not assessed
4.3, next review 2026-10-01, -14 days from the as-of date
6.1.3, next review 2027-06-12, 240 days from the as-of date
explanation: Clause 4.3 is the one row with a review date behind the as-of date. 6.1.2 reads review due soon true, and 7.2 and 6.1.3 read both flags false. The summary prints reviews overdue 1.

prompt: Who may lead the planned internal audit over 8.1, 8.2, 9.1.1 and 9.2 with the scope left as it is?
options: u-tari, whose one clause in the scope is Conformant
u-nneka, since clause 9.2 is the internal audit clause
u-chidi, or an external lead auditor named in text
u-kalu, once another examiner records 8.1 and 8.2
explanation: Both of those rows read ALLOWED. u-tari owns 9.1.1, u-nneka 9.2 and u-kalu 8.1 and 8.2, and each is refused for owning a clause in the scope, whatever that clause's status.

prompt: The planner drops 8.1 and 8.2 from the planned audit's scope so that u-kalu can lead it. What happens to clause 8.1's coverage row?
options: Nothing moves: 8.1 keeps last examined 2024-05-16 from ISA-2024-001 until a counting audit examines it again.
8.1 reads never, because a clause taken out of an audit's scope loses its examination history.
8.1 reads stale, because a clause dropped from a planned scope lapses to before the cycle.
8.1 reads covered by the new audit as soon as it is planned, whether or not it is in scope.
explanation: Coverage reads the latest examination by a Reported or Closed internal audit. At a cycle of 3 years 8.1 reads covered true from ISA-2024-001, and a plan that is not yet reported moves no date.

prompt: A member of an audit team is refused by canExamineClause. What does that refusal ask for?
options: That the scope drop the clause the member owns before the audit starts.
That another member of the audit records the result for that clause.
That the lead auditor countersign the result before it is recorded.
That the clause owner in the register be changed to somebody else first.
explanation: The examiner refusal ends "so somebody else on the audit has to record this result." It offers no change of scope; that remedy is the lead auditor refusal's, together with a change of auditor.

prompt: Which of these pairings of an app with the name its independence check reads is correct?
options: Audit & Findings Manager: the lead auditor against the auditee
Document Control: the reviewer against the owner of the clause
ISO register: the lead auditor against the auditee of the audit
Audit & Findings Manager: each examiner against the clause owner
explanation: Three records, three names: clause owners for the ISO register, the auditee for the Audit & Findings Manager, the revision's author for Document Control. u-adaeze, author of rev-0019-10, is refused as its reviewer.

prompt: The certification body's surveillance audit examined clause 6.1.2 in 2026. Why is 6.1.2 still among the clauses never examined?
options: Its surveillance result was Conformant, and only a Nonconformant result counts as an examination.
6.1.2 is Partially conformant, and coverage leaves out any clause without a full verdict recorded.
Only Internal audits count, and no internal audit has examined 6.1.2.
The surveillance audit is still waiting for its report, so its results do not count yet.
explanation: COVERING_AUDIT_TYPES holds the one word Internal. ISA-2026-S01 examined 6.1.2, Conformant on 2026-07-22, and the coverage row for 6.1.2 still reads last examined never, by audit none.

prompt: Which ORASHI audits count towards coverage?
options: ISA-2026-001 and ISA-2026-002, the two still open
All five of the Internal audits, whatever their status
explanation: Two Closed internal audits and one Reported one. ISA-2026-S01 fails on its type, ISA-2026-002 (In progress) and ISA-2025-003 (Cancelled) on their status.

prompt: What separates a stale clause from a never examined one?
options: A stale clause was examined by a Surveillance audit; a never examined clause by nobody at any time.
A stale clause had a counting examination before the cycle began; a never examined clause had none at all.
A stale clause failed its last examination; a never examined clause was not reached by its audit.
A stale clause is past its review date; a never examined clause has no review date on the register.
explanation: Clause 4.3, last examined 2023-09-20, reads stale true. Clauses 6.1.2, 7.2 and 7.5.3 read never with stale false. The list ranks them apart: never examined blocking, stale serious.

prompt: ISO 45001:2018 clause 6.1.2, last examined 2025-10-14, reads stale under its own cycle. Read against ISO 14001:2015's cycle instead, what would the same date have shown?
options: never examined, since a borrowed cycle drops the examination
covered, as ISO 14001:2015 clause 8.1 reads from that very date
stale all the same, since the examination date alone decides
covered and stale together, one flag for each standard's cycle
explanation: A date that falls outside a 1 year window can still fall inside a 3 year one, and the digest shows it: from 2025-10-14, the ISO 14001:2015 row prints covered true. That is the case for reading a mixed register by standard.

prompt: At a cycle of 1 year, what does the ORASHI coverage table print?
options: covered 8, stale 1, never examined 3
covered 9, stale 0, never examined 3
covered 6, stale 0, never examined 6
covered 6, stale 3, never examined 3
explanation: The rows read 1 year: 6, 3, 3; 2 years: 6, 3, 3; 3 years: 8, 1, 3; 4 years: 9, 0, 3. Never examined does not move with the cycle.

prompt: Clause 5.2's latest counting result is an Observation. Does 5.2 read covered?
options: No: an Observation records a remark and is not a verdict on the clause.
No: the clause stays uncovered until the observation is closed as a finding.
Yes, though only once ISA-2026-002 reports its later Conformant result.
Yes: the examination on 2026-06-09 is inside the cycle, whatever it found.
explanation: Coverage records that a counting audit looked at the clause inside the cycle, and the result is read elsewhere. An Observation on 5.2 and a Nonconformant result on 6.1.3 both read covered true.

prompt: Which ORASHI finding does canCloseFinding allow at 2026-10-15?
options: ISF-2026-005, which may close on its action ac3
ISF-2026-001, which may close a second time
ISF-2026-003, which may close with nothing more recorded
ISF-2026-002, which may close again once voided
explanation: ISF-2026-005 is refused for want of its correction, ISF-2026-004 for its open action, ISF-2026-001 as already closed and ISF-2026-002 as already voided. An Opportunity for improvement is no nonconformity.

prompt: A corrective action on a Major nonconformity is checked and found not to have worked. What does the engine ask for?
options: The correction recorded again, since the instance has come back.
The root cause changed to Other, since the first cause was wrong.
The finding downgraded to a Minor nonconformity so it can close.
Another corrective action, raised in place of closing over the one that failed.
explanation: "A corrective action here was checked and found not to have worked. Raise another one rather than closing over it." Only a corrective action verified effective closes a Major nonconformity.

prompt: On an NCR in the quality module, which record plays the part a correction plays on a finding?
options: The corrective action, which deals with the cause
The root cause, which names the category of failure
The effectiveness check, which proves the fix worked
The disposition, which deals with the item
explanation: The quality module's words: "A disposition deals with the item; a corrective action deals with the cause." A disposition is to a nonconforming item what a correction is to a finding.

prompt: A cause recorded as Measurement or inspection on an NCR and one recorded as Measurement or monitoring on a finding: how should a reader count them?
options: As one category, since both of them describe a measurement failure.
As the ISO category, since the quality list is a subset of the ISO list.
As Other, since neither list holds the other list's word for it.
As two categories from two lists, each quoted in its own list's words.
explanation: Measurement or inspection is only in the quality list of 9; Measurement or monitoring and Management system are only in the ISO list of 10. The quality list is no subset of the ISO list.

prompt: ISF-2026-001 was raised 2026-02-03 and closed 2026-04-21. What happens to its age as the as-of date moves later?
options: It grows by one each day, in the same way an open finding's age grows.
It resets to zero at closure.
It grows until its due date, 2026-04-30.
It stays fixed, since it answers how long the finding took to close.
explanation: A closed or voided finding stops ageing at its closed date. The three open findings, raised 2026-06-12, read 125 at 2026-10-15 and keep growing.

prompt: Which ORASHI finding sorts first in findingByUrgency, and at which rank?
options: ISF-2026-003 at rank 0, the open finding with the earliest raised date
ISF-2026-001 at rank 1, the Major nonconformity raised earliest of all
ISF-2026-004 at rank 0, an open Major nonconformity that is overdue
ISF-2026-005 at rank 2, the open finding whose due date falls latest
explanation: Rank 0 is an open Major nonconformity that is overdue, and ISF-2026-004, due 2026-09-30, is the only finding reading overdue true. ISF-2026-003 and ISF-2026-005 both rank 3, and ISF-2026-001 ranks 4.

prompt: An audit reads Fieldwork complete and its planned end has passed. Is it overdue?
options: No, as its fieldwork is done
Yes, in both modules
Only in auditManagement
No, only Planned and In progress are
explanation: isAuditOverdue reads Fieldwork complete true in isoCompliance and in auditManagement. AUDIT_UNDELIVERED_STATUSES holds Planned, In progress and Fieldwork complete; an audit is overdue only while it is undelivered.

prompt: A certificate has 91 days left to run. What do its two flags read, and what does the list carry for it?
options: Both flags false, and no certificate item on the list.
certificateExpiring true, and a watch item on the list.
certificateExpiring true, and no item on the list yet.
Both flags false, and a watch item counting the days.
explanation: The lead window is 90 days, so a certificate one day beyond it raises neither flag. Moved one day nearer, to 2027-01-13, the row reads certificateExpiring true with a watch item.

prompt: A certificate reads certificateDays -15. Which flag reads true?
options: certificateExpiring alone, until the recertification audit is booked
certificateExpired alone, since rule R3 keeps the two apart
certificateExpired and certificateExpiring, both of them
Neither flag, since certificateDays below 0 reads null
explanation: Rule R3: expired and expiring are two separate flags, and a certificate at -15 reads certificateExpiring false and certificateExpired true. Under Q6 an expired certificate is a serious readiness item.

prompt: Which three items does the ORASHI readiness list rank serious?
options: the stale clause, the clause never assessed and the overdue action
the open Major, the never examined clauses and the unevidenced claim
the minor nonconformity, the past-due review and the overdue finding
the stale clause, the overdue finding and the certificate item
explanation: The serious items read: 1 clause last audited before this certification cycle began, 1 applicable clause never assessed, and 1 corrective or preventive action past its due date.

prompt: Why does certification readiness print no percentage?
options: Any weighting between items is an opinion, and a high score can hide one blocker.
The engine does not hold the counts that a percentage would need to be formed.
A percent rounds half up and would hide a blocker whose share falls below one half.
The certificate is a gate over the list, and a percentage has no way to show a gate.
explanation: The first blocking item says it: "A certification body will not recommend certification over one." A list counts and names every item and averages nothing away.

prompt: The watch item "1 minor nonconformity is open." stands on the ORASHI list. Which finding is behind it, and what keeps that finding from closing?
options: ISF-2026-003, with an action still open
ISF-2026-005, which has no correction recorded yet
ISF-2026-004, which has no corrective action verified effective
ISF-2026-002, which was voided before its correction was recorded
explanation: openMinor 1 is ISF-2026-005, due 2026-12-11. canCloseFinding refuses it with the correction sentence: "Record the correction: what was done about the thing that was found." ISF-2026-004 is the open Major, a blocking item.

prompt: The blocking item for never-examined clauses cites which requirement?
options: ISO 14001:2015 §9.2: the organization audits its own system
ISO 19011, which bars an auditor from auditing their own work
ISO 9001:2015 §4.3, which keeps a justification for an exclusion
ISO 14001:2015 §9.2, which calls for certification body surveillance
explanation: "3 applicable clauses have never been examined by an internal audit. ISO 14001:2015 §9.2 requires the organization to audit its own system." This is why a surveillance audit moves no clause's date.

prompt: Which readiness count and summary count print the same figure for the same thing under two names?
options: openMajor 1 and open findings 3
evidenced 9 and unevidenced claims 1
covered 8 and clauses covered 8
staleAudited 1 and reviews overdue 1
explanation: Never audited 3 and neverAudited 3 are another such pair. staleAudited 1 is clause 4.3's coverage and reviews overdue 1 is clause 4.3's review: equal figures, two different counts.

prompt: Owner decisions Q4, Q5 and Q6 each show up in one module of this tier. Which pairing is right?
options: Q4 independence, Q5 coverage, Q6 findings
Q4 findings, Q5 coverage, Q6 the claim register
Q4 coverage, Q5 independence, Q6 readiness
Q4 readiness, Q5 findings, Q6 independence
explanation: Q4: ISO coverage counts only Reported or Closed audits. Q5: every examiner is checked for independence. Q6: an expired certificate is a serious readiness item, one inside the lead window a watch item.

prompt: An app shows no overdue review for a document. Which held limit should stop a reader taking that at face value?
options: A templated audit with no checklist items passes the unanswered-items rule vacuously.
A complete programme containing a cancelled audit reads below one hundred percent.
A missing review period makes nextReviewDate return a date 24 months after issue.
A date that could not be read is refused in one module only, so a clean screen elsewhere proves nothing.
explanation: Of the four held limits this is the one a screen hides: an empty overdue list looks the same whether its date was read or not. The other three limits concern templates, programmes and a certificate.

prompt: Rule R1 puts one rule behind three exports. What does that rule decide?
options: Whether an audit is outstanding, for programmeProgress, summarise and canCompleteProgramme alike
Whether an audit is overdue, for isoCompliance and auditManagement alike
Whether a percent rounds up, for each of the three exports that print one
Whether a sentence names its standard, for every refusal that is returned
explanation: On four audits with one cancelled and no reason, programmeProgress counts 2 outstanding and summarise counts 2. The overdue rule for audits is the ASC-1 rule, a separate one.

prompt: An obligation with no lead time set reads Due soon. What does its reason say?
options: That it is inside the default lead time, and that none is set for this obligation.
That it is due soon, with nothing said about which lead time was applied.
That a lead time must be recorded before any status can be derived.
That it reads On track, since only a recorded lead time starts Due soon.
explanation: The ASC-1 rule: the Due soon reason says when the default lead time applies, as REG-2026-012's reason does. complianceStatus.DEFAULT_LEAD_TIME_DAYS is the default it names.

prompt: A golden figure sits beside an engine figure and the two agree. What has that shown?
options: That the engine was run twice with one result.
Two methods agreeing, one of them an independent Python oracle.
That the refusal sentence beside the figure is correct word for word.
That the figure matches a published standard's own worked example.
explanation: Each golden file is written by an independent stdlib Python oracle from the rules as the modules and the status document state them. The oracles check a gate's verdict and never its wording.

prompt: The isoCompliance oracle carries 1 sort case. What does the digest leave unsaid about it?
options: Whether it passed or failed
Which module it belongs to
Which ordering it checks
Nothing; it names the sort
explanation: The digest states findingByUrgency's rule and prints each finding's rank, and does not say which ordering the isoCompliance sort case checks. Where the digest stops, an expert says so.

prompt: Which of these does this course own?
options: Risk scores, risk bands and heat maps
The Management of Change approval gates
Audit independence and the root cause categories
How a lesson learned is written and approved
explanation: This course owns audit independence in both forms, the audit and finding lifecycles and the root cause categories. The other three belong to riskchange, "Risk, Change & Learning".

prompt: Why does canSetClauseStatus ask for the assessor's name as well as the date?
options: The name decides which of the two root cause lists the clause's cause is recorded against.
Without a name, a verdict cannot be checked against the clause owner for independence.
The name sets the clause's next review date, counted from the day of assessment.
The name is what the certification body counts when it reads the coverage table.
explanation: A verdict with no date cannot be placed in a cycle, and one with no name cannot be checked against the owner of the clause. canExamineClause refuses u-kalu recording 8.1, which u-kalu owns.

prompt: Which clause does the serious item "1 clause was last audited before this certification cycle began." point at, and what was its last counting examination?
explanation: Clause 4.3 reads stale true, at -1121 days. 8.1 is covered at 3 years, and 6.1.2 and 7.5.3 were examined only by audits that do not count, so both read never.

prompt: ac4 is Preventive, Complete, with no effectiveness verdict. Where does it show in the ORASHI counts?
options: In the summary's awaiting an effectiveness check 1
In the summary's overdue actions 1, as its due date 2026-09-01 has passed
In the summary's open actions 2, counted beside ac1
Nowhere, since a Complete action leaves every count
explanation: The summary's open actions 2 are ac1 and ac3, and overdue actions 1 is ac1. ac4 reads open false and overdue false, and the digest names it as the action awaiting an effectiveness check.

prompt: How does canCloseFinding in the Audit & Findings Manager relate to canCloseFinding in the ISO register?
options: The Audit & Findings Manager's copy skips the effectiveness check on a Major.
They agree on Majors and differ on Minors.
The ISO version asks for an independent examiner before it closes a finding.
They are one function, so a finding closes by one rule in both apps.
explanation: One function object serves both apps, so the Major walk, with its correction, root cause, corrective action and effectiveness check, is the same walk in each. isoCompliance.isActionOverdue is likewise the quality module's isCapaOverdue.

prompt: What does rule R5 guarantee a reader of a refusal or of a readiness sentence?
options: That it cites a numbered clause of whichever standard it names.
That it names the standard of the register it was read against.
That the oracle has checked its wording word for word.
That it names ISO 19011 whenever a person is refused.
explanation: The ORASHI list carries 1 item naming ISO 14001:2015 and 0 naming ISO 9001. Only the ISO 9001:2015 Not applicable refusal cites a numbered clause, §4.3.

prompt: Which one action on the record would remove the serious item about a clause never assessed at all?
options: Auditing clause 7.2 in an internal audit and reporting the audit that examined it
Assessing clause 7.2 and recording its verdict with a date and an assessor
Recording an evidence reference against clause 5.2 in the register
Setting 7.2 to Not applicable while its applicability reads Applicable
explanation: Clause 7.2 reads Not assessed. An internal audit would clear its blocking never-examined item and leave the verdict missing, and setting Not applicable with applicability unchanged is refused.
